notes.rationale: Bambara requires the pronoun a before the second verb; Hebrew builds the subject into the verb form

notes.subject: Fa!
notes.rationale: הנה summons the listener to look — a direct call to attention

notes.subject: ירום ונשא וגבה
notes.rationale: three near-synonymous verbs of rising piled in ascent; Bambara keeps three verbs but the Hebrew climb of height-verbs is flattened

translation: Fa! n denbaga bɛna baara kɛ ni hakilijagoya ye; a bɛna kun bonya, ⟨a⟩ bɛna ɲɛsin sanfɛ, a bɛna ka bonya kosɛbɛ.
